q7.answer: The client does not hold the key. On every outbound call it runs secrets.get('<name>'), which takes the lock briefly and returns the current string from the in-memory dictionary, and builds the Authorization header from that. The refresh thread swaps the value and version id together under the same lock, so the next request uses the new key with no restart.

q8.answer: Step 8 is a check by the security on-call or release engineer. The cluster must list exactly the expected 4 pods, all on the post-migration image. For each pod and each of the three names, the latest 'secret loaded name=<name> version=<id>' log line must equal the store's current version id. The pod must have no refresh-failure warning after that line. Any missing or mismatched pod blocks revocation. Evidence is recorded on the ticket, and pre-migration images are blocked in step 9 before the revoke.

q9.answer: Order: (1) check providers support two active keys; (2) set store access and KMS, and verify it; (3) issue new keys at the providers (old stay active) and copy them into the store; (4) and (5) switch the app to read from the store and remove the keys from the YAML, with the CI guard, in the same PR; (7) rolling deploy; (8) confirm all pods are on the new keys; (9) block old images, then revoke the old keys at the providers. Rotation is therefore split: new keys are created before the code change, and old keys are revoked last.

q10.answer: make run starts the app with APP_ENV=dev and reads orders-api/dev/* from the store with the engineer's own store login. Those are provider sandbox or test keys, not prod keys. The deny rule in step 2 stops an engineer from reading prod even with APP_ENV=prod. A make run-offline target points the clients at local stubs and needs no store access or keys.

q11.answer: Any failure to read any of the three secrets counts as a startup failure, including a missing secret or access denied. The app makes 1 initial attempt and retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart. It then logs the secret name and error class, never a value, and exits non-zero. It never becomes ready with only two keys, because /healthz returns 503 until all three are loaded. I did not separately decide whether a missing secret should skip the retries, so it is retried like any other failure.
